preview: Interview experience for an internship role at BNY Mellon consisting of an online assessment, offline PPT, a pure technical interview round, and a resume/HR interview round.
content:
Interview experience
Tvisha Vedant
Branch CS
BNY mellon
Stipend : 75k per month
Overview
The process was :
OA (4 DSA q )
offline PPT
Results of OA
Interview 1 tech 1 HR

1
OA
The OA consisted of 4 questions :
1)
An escape game requires that players solve various puzzles to obtain objects that will
aid them in escaping. In one such puzzle. players are given an array of integers and a
set of rules to follow in order. Here are the instructions given to the players: "Given an
array of integer values, maximize the points earned using the following method.
1.
Choose a value v. Delete all elements of that value and add their sum to the points.
2.
Delete all elements equal to v 1 or v7 for no points
3.
Repeat steps 1 and 2 until there are no more elements in the array.
Calculate the maximum number of points that can be achieved by following these rules
for an array of values. Example elements (5, 6, 6.4, 11 Delete 11 for 11 points. Since
there are no elements equal to 11-1- 10 or 11+1=12, proceed with the remaining
elements (5, 6, 6, 4]. Delete the two 6s for 12 more points. Delete any elements equal to
6-1=5 or 6+1=7. Then proceed with the remaining elements: [4]. Finally delete the 4 and
add 4 points for total points 11+12+4=27.
Function Description :
You were supposed to complete a function which had the following parameter(s) : int
elements[n]: an array of integers
it expected us to return long int: the maximum number of points that can be earned
Ig this question is on leetcode do check it out once...
2)
A subarray is a contiguous portion of an array, Given an array of Integers, determine the
number of distinct subarrays that can be formed having at most a given number of odd
elements. Two subarrays are district if they differ at even one position in their contents.
Example:
numbers [1, 2, 3, 4]
The following is a list of the 8 distinct valid subarrays having no more than 1 odd
element: [[1], [2], [3], [4], [1,2], [2, 3], [3, 4], [2, 3, 4]]
Function Description:

2
int numbers[n]: an array of integers int k: the maximum number of odd elements that can
be in a subarray
Return int: the number of distinct subarrays that can be formed as described
Constraints ig it was this not sure
1<= n <= 1000
1 <= k <=n
1 <= numbers[i] <= 250
3)
Given a list of employees where each is assigned a numeric evaluation score, use the
selection process below to find the sum of scores of selected employees
1.
The employee with the highest score among the first k employees or last & employees in
the score list are selected.
2.
The selected employee is removed from the score list.
3.
The process continues to select the next employee until the team size is achieved.
Note:
1.
In case multiple employees have the same highest score, the employee with the lowest
Index is selected.
2.
If there are fewer than kemployees, the entire list is available for selection.
Example score [10, 20, 10, 15, 5, 30, 20]
teamSize= 2 k= 3
• For the first selection, choose from the first 3 elements [10, 20, 10] or the last 3 elements: [5,
30, 20] . Score 30 is selected and removed from the list. This makes score = [10, 20, 10, 15, 5,
20] For the second selection, choose from [10, 20, 10] or [15, 5, 20] . Score 20 is selected from
the lowest index and removed from the list. This makes score = [10, 10, 15, 5, 20] The sum of
the selected employees' scores is 30+20=50.
4 )
A virtual memory grid represents a computer's memory management. The grid comprises nrows
and m columns of cells, where the content of each memory cell (0, j) is denoted by mem[i][j].
where 0 <= i < n 0 <= j < m This memory management system operates as follows:

3
• Memory Access: Memory access begins from the top-left cell (0, 0). For every memory cell (t,
j) there is an option to either access the data in the current cell (i, j) or proceed to the next cell
by moving one cell right (1, j + 1 ) or one cell down (t + 1, j) provided that such cells exist within
the grid.
The objective is to reach the bottom-right cell (n - 1, m - 1 ) to complete the data retrieval.
Data Retrieval: During memory access, data stored in a cell can be read or skipped.
Memory Usage Limitation: No more than k data items can be read from a row.
Determine the maximum sum of data that can be retrieved considering the per row read limit.
Example It is given that mem =[ [3, 4, 10] , [2, 8, 1] ], and k = 2 Only 2 cells can be read in a row.
In row 0, for instance, cell pairs are (3, 4), (3, 10), (4, 10).
The optimal way to move will be from (0, 0) -> (0, 1) -> (1, 1) (1, . 2), reading the data from
every cell visited The sum of data retrieved is 3 + 4 + 8 + 1 = 16 .
No path exists from (0, 0) ^ + to (1, 2) to collect a greater sum of data .
The PPT
The results were announced on the interview day after their ppt, which everyone had to
attend compulsorily. It's very important to attend the ppt and try to note down points
which might be important for the interview.
Participate in the ppt if possible give answers ask questions when given a chance
This really did help me but again not being able to do this doesn't mean you will not get
the internship but if you can grab the opportunity go for it.
The names of every interviewer is really important to remember when you enter the
interview room and greet them with their name like hello Tvisha.
Interviews
There were 2 interviews one was a pure tech based round the second was conducted by
a senior person which involved questions related to projects on your resume and general
HR questions

4
Interview1(Pure Tech)
I greeted her as hello Asha! smiled and took a seat.
She started with asking with are you excited to which I replied yes and
I wasn't asked to introduce myself
But it's very important to have a good introduction ready as it's asked in most interviews.
Also the points you collect for the introduction can always be used for the HR round later.
Then she moved on to ask me about my language of preference to which I replied cpp
for DSA and that I am familiar with python as I have used it in my projects
She asked me why I preferred cpp
First I told her that it is a very fast language
And I told her that it's a lower level language compared to python and the industry works
on the basis of time. There are cases where instruments like ATM machines use
assembly to increase speed by milliseconds .
I then paused for a second as I thought that this is one of the most important point
in my opinion she then asked if is that it??
Then I added that it is also a language that supports OOPs.
So she then asked me to explain OOPs
I immediately started with explanation of the 4 pillars first naming them all
(I would suggest not to do this) We should explain what it really means and then move
on to the 4 pillars.
I explained her encapsulation and polymorphism for polymorphism I explained about
runtime and compile time polymorphism by mentioning static and dynamic allocation and
then abstraction upon completion of the explanation of abstraction. She asked me to
explain the difference between abstraction and encapsulation. i really do not remember
what I said here as I hadn't completely prepared for this question but I did give a
reasonable answer.
She then told me to write down an example in code about abstraction. There are many
options to explain abstraction. I opted to explain it using access specifiers by taking the
example of a bank with a few private members and public members in the base class.

5
Here I was asked some questions related to accessing private members of base class in
public class. The answer was setter getter methods .
She then asked about constructors I explained that to her and I added if any type of
constructor is declared by us the compiler doesn't even declare a default constructor and
that it's best practice to declare a default constructor she then asked why is that so I
didn't know the concrete answer to it but I used my reasoning and told that maybe the
requirement would never be of a default constructor if it's declared otherwise and hence
to avoid anomalies which might arise due to a false usage of default constructors in
places where not required this would have been the workaround.
I was then asked some question in context of the example I had given for abstraction
which was related to the concept of 'super' a concept present in Java and python and not
in cpp I wasn't aware about it and tried to think out loud and ask questions in its context
to interviewer but then I told I am not aware of the concept which will be required for the
solution. She then asked me if I am aware about the concept of super to which I replied
no. Be honest and tell them that you are unaware of stuff if you cannot get an answer.
It's better than blurting random things which might display loopholes in your
understanding of the concepts you are aware of .
Later she moved on to DSA. I wasn't happy with the interview so far as I was not able to
answer the question related to super and had fumbled while giving the answer related to
setter and getter methods. But I didn't let that feeling be visible on my face and body
language and kept a calm composure.
She asked me if I was aware of various sorting techniques and asked me to name one
which I would like to explain to which I replied merge sort.
She gave a plain sheet of paper and told me to write the pseudo code and explain it with
a dry run to the example she had given, usually interviewers look at what we are doing
and it's a good practice to think out loud while writing the code but my interview insisted
to just complete the work and then explain it all together and started doing something on
her laptop I didn't like this at all but had to continue as she had instructed to do so..
I took some time to write the pseudo code but did not do a dry run first on my own to
save time and went with it I had forgotten a i++ and j++ condition at a place in the merge
function which I added during the dry run and I had also mistakened the position of mid
while explaining a sub problem which also I corrected in a second, she was confusing me
at every point but I stayed confident.

6
Then she asked me about the time complexity and derive the same, I made the recursion
tree and told her the time complexity
She then asked me about the number of merge function calls being made in my example
which was 3 I just answered by looking at the recursion tree which was of height 3
Then she asked to prove if the time complexity formula is correct by giving the same for
the dry run example.
The no. of merge function calls which each will work for a constant time is the time
complexity so that will be 3 here. So I answered yes the TC formula is correct log 5 will
be 3. as no. of elements in the array were 5.
She asked me if log5 is 3 here I had got panicked as I forgot it's to the base 2 and not
10 so I just said yes and that I am not aware of the exact value of log5 at this point I had
lost my cool and was not completely in my senses because log 5 to the base 2 has to
be approximately 3 as 2^2 is 4 .
Later she asked me about searching algorithms I know about to which I replied binary
search
She asked me why I prefer binary search to which I explained how a problem gets
divided into just half at every step and hence it's an optimal approach. And the TC is
logN
I was then asked if I am aware of 'postorder' inorder traversal and she gave an infix
expression (I got a bit puzzled at first and was thinking where to use binary trees )
and told me to convert it into postfix and also give the code for it .
I did convert it to postfix. She again tried to confuse and puzzle me but I stayed
confident..as while writing the previous DSA question there had been a 4-7 min of
silence.
I didn't want it again so instead of first writing the entire code I explained the
entire logic to her to which she agreed and then I went on to write the code when I was
halfway she asked for an update had a look at the sheet and asked how we can
modularise the conditions to which I agreed and then she told it's ok you are done thank
you...
She didn't even ask me if I had any questions and just told me to leave. I was completely
heartbroken and shocked.

7
I didn't expect to be shortlisted for the second round and while people were either getting
rejected or being sent for the second round I was not being updated about anything. My
first round ended at about 2pm and my second round started after 5:30 , until then I was
just waiting and roaming around in TPO helping friends out talking with people…
OOPs was asked to everyone , DSA included sorting techniques, questions related to
binary search , trees , a friend was asked to implement some time scheduling algorithm
of OS and AVL trees check Kindips experience for that ...
Interview 2(Resume/Tech + HR )
This included quite chill questions on resume projects
He first asked me about my first interview i.e. the tech interview to which I replied it was
good but I wanted it to be extremely perfect as I was very keen on getting into BNY
and then I added that there were ups and downs but it did meet my expectations in the end .
( As it's important to show confidence in ourselves at every point in an interview as it can
change the interviewer opinion on you. )
He went through my resume.
I was asked about a healthcare chatbot project which was first in my resume (it was
done by me during project x ) , which I explained to him entirely in a minute with the
unique features it had.. He asked me about RAG which was mentioned in the project
description.
He also noticed that my pointers at that time were 9.19 and asked why it was so less (idk
why he thought this was less 😂maybe he was testing how I would respond). I told him
that during second year handling projects and academics was a bit new for me and
hence it took me time to learn how to manage my time properly for everything and hence
academics got a bit affected and that I have learnt how to manage things now and
everything is well and my pointers will grow again..
Then he asked me why I wanted to join bny. I mentioned my new interest in finance and
excitement to explore new possibilities linked with llms data analysis and finance in the
future…

8
Followed by the question he asked that I had no significant development or Java
experience on my resume but that might be the work I will do in my internship to which I
emphasized on quick learning and that I can grasp things quickly he asked me how I
learn things, I explained this by taking an example of learning react for a project.
Then he asked me about my flexibility to move to Pune and I was able to convince him
properly. He then asked if I had any questions I don't remember exactly what I asked (ig
it was something about the freedom interns have on working with technologies of their
choice or something similar.) but the discussion then took a turn with me giving the
example of my gsoc project that even though the datasets I worked with and the context
I had to give the LLM was of neuroscience background I did adjust in that. I then said
that the ppt was very much enough to answer the questions I had in the morning and
hence I do not have any further questions .
Also I had already asked one question during the ppt so I ended the interview by telling
that I look forward to work with BNY 🙂
Results:
Results were declared on the same day offline in front of us..
Preparation
●
DSA : follow 450 sheet by love babar or striver but this needs to be done 3-4
months prior if less time use neetcode 150 and the arrays , binary search ,
strings part of the bigger sheets should be covered for sure.
●
OOPs DBMS OS : interview bit , whimsical mind maps and javatpoint for oops
and w3schools for sql basics.
●
Ask for your senior's help to get at least one mock interview done, I had got a lot
of tips from my seniors and i had given both the rounds of HILTI on-campus drive
but then had got rejected 🙃..but it did give me a good mock interview
experience.
●
Good formal attire is important.
●
Prepare the details related to the company and take notes during their PPT.
All the best !!!! Yall can reach out to me on linkedin anytime if help is needed !! 🙂
